summary: The root فري (fry) describes a lamb or its skin, or a kid's skin, being roasted until its upper parts become dried up. This term is found in Q. 3.
lane: Q. 3 اِفْرَنْبَجَ ذ , said of a lamb, (Lth, O,) or of the skin of a lamb, (S, K, [some of the copies of the latter of which have الجَمَل in the place of الحَمَل ,]) and of the skin of a kid, (O,) It was roasted so that the upper parts of it became dried up. (Lth, S, O, K.)

provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: (M, K,) aor. يَفْرِيهِ, (K,) inf. n. فَرْىٌ, (K,) He slit it, or cut it lengthwise, ill, or improperly; or well, or properly; as also and [both relating to both of the foregoing explanations]: (K:) or he slit it, or cut it lengthwise, and made it bad, or improper; as also: or, accord.
فَرَّىَ see 1, first quarter, in three places.
أَفْرَىَ see 1, former half, in seven places: and also in the latter half, near the middle of the paragraph.

It became slit, or cut lengthwise; (S, M, Msb, K;) as also; (S, M, Msb;) both said of a skin, (M,) or of a thing: (S:) or it became much slit, or rent; said of the sewing of a leathern water-skin. (T.) And تفرّى عَنْهُ ثَوْبُهُ His garment became much slit, or rent, from him. (T.) And تفرّت العَيْنُ (tropical:) The spring of water burst forth: (K, TA:) or تفرّت الأَرْضُ بِالعُيُونِ (tropical:) The earth, or ground, burst with the springs.
إِنْفَرَىَ see the next preceding paragraph.

إِفْتَرَىَ افترىكَ ِبًا He forged, or fabricated, a lie, or falsehood; (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K;) you say, افترى عَلَيْهِ كَ ِبًا [ he forged against him a lie ]; (Mgh, Msb;) and كَ ِبًا signifies the same, (T, S, M, Msb, K,) aor. يَفْرِى, (Msb,) inf. n. فَرْىٌ; (M;) and this verb likewise is followed by عَلَيْهِ: (Msb:) in this sense is mentioned as said by Lth; others saying افترى. (T.) افترى is used in the Kur in relation also to the attributing a copartner to God: thus in the saying [in iv.

Clamour; or a confusion, or mixture, of cries or shouts or noises. (M, K, TA. [ الحَلْبَةُ in the CK is a mistake for الجَلَبَةُ.]) فِرْيَةٌ A lie, or falsehood; (S, * M, Mgh, * Msb, * K, TA;) a subst. from اِفْتَرَى: (S, Mgh, Msb, TA:) and meaning [also] a defamation: (Mgh:) pl. فِرًى. (TA.) And An affair, or a case, of great magnitude or moment or gravity. (M, TA.)

Slit, or cut lengthwise; applied to a skin ( جِلْدٌ ): and so فَرِيَّةٌ [app. as applied to a قِرْبَة or the like, as being fem. of فَرِىٌّ ]. (M, TA.) And A wide دَلْو [or leathern bucket]; (M, K;) as though it were slit; (M;) as also فَرِيَّةٌ. (K.) And A thing forged, or fabricated; (S, K, TA;) thus [or rather as hence meaning unknown, or unheard of, ] in the saying, لَقَدْجِئْتِ شَيْئًا فَرِيًّا, in the Kur [xix. 28], (S, TA,) i. e.
أَفْرَى الفِرَى occurs in a trad. as meaning The most lying of lies: الفِرَى is the pl. of فِرْيَةٌ. (TA.)
A مَزَادَة [or leathern water-bag] made in a good, or proper, manner; well made. (T, TA.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
